config_name: MacBook Pro 14-inch — M5 Pro 18-core CPU / 20-core GPU, 24GB RAM, 1TB SSD

specs.keyboard_notes: Magic Keyboard, Touch ID, Force Touch trackpad

battery.notes: Up to 22h video / 14h web claimed; 72.4Wh. Higher GPU tier draws slightly more under load.

price.notes: Verified on apple.com/ca buy page (see research/parts/apple/NOTES.md).

reviews.quote: noticeable performance advantages over the previous M4 Pro chip (~20 % CPU, 30-50 % GPU) (same chip family tested in the 16-inch chassis)
exceptional battery life... lasts well over a full day (same chassis, M5 model tested)

praises: The 20-core GPU turns 30-50% higher GPU scores over M4 Pro into real timeline and render gains (NBC)
18-core CPU chews through compile and transcode jobs that stall the 12-core M6 (NBC benchmarks)
Thunderbolt 5 + PCIe 5.0 SSD for fast docks and storage (NBC)
Only +$250 CAD over the 15-core tier — the best performance-per-dollar step on the 14-inch ladder
complaints: The 14-inch chassis runs the 18-core part hotter than the 16-inch does (NBC thermal behaviour on 14-inch Max models)
Prices are still high, especially when you add upgrades (NBC con)
Still no SD Express support in the card reader (NBC con)
RAM and SSD soldered; 24GB base with paid tiers to 48/64GB
Same 5-year-old chassis; a redesign is overdue (NBC and Tom's Hardware)

design_philosophy: The full-power M5 Pro in the small chassis: Apple's answer for users who want near-Max multicore and a 20-core GPU without carrying 2.1 kg. It compresses workstation-class throughput into 1.6 kg at the cost of earlier thermal limits.
rating_notes: Ratings inferred from NBC's 92.3% M5 Pro review (16-inch chassis): +0.4 gaming / +0.4 creative_work / +0.4 ai_ml for the 20-core GPU tier, −0.4 thermals_noise and −0.2 battery for the higher-power chip in the smaller 72.4Wh chassis.
